summary.prose: S3 adds the standalone module's authoritative memory store in a dedicated memory.lance directory. One qualified table mutation publishes memory transitions, provenance, replay/deletion protection, a receipt and generation together; retries reconcile that receipt before reapplying effects. Scoped reads use a pinned committed version and a final freshness check. Native crash durability and cross-platform behavior are mandatory build gates; the recorded macOS normal-exit probe establishes only basic SDK compatibility.

hldContextSlice.frameworkSummary: Choose a1: ports-and-adapters library with optional local service host. The library owns one queue, one context-builder processing loop and one dedicated Lance connection per resolved data directory. Admission, project policy and source identity are common to both hosts. Standalone and embedded execution must pass the same behavioral and failure suite. [[c1]] [[c2]]

ownedContracts.name: Single-writer atomic memory commit
ownedContracts.purpose: Bind canonical transitions, provenance, generation, deletion protection and processing outcome in a qualified single-table commit.

consumedContracts.name: Host ports and package lifecycle
consumedContracts.purpose: Versioned dependency boundary for independent embedded execution; no backend imports, implicit globals or ownership of supplied providers. All module model requests use a module-local dispatcher; supplied ports do not imply an existing daemon-wide scheduler.

consumedContracts.name: Application service and domain wire types
consumedContracts.purpose: One versioned typed command/query model shared by embedded, IPC and insrc adapters; all mutation paths enqueue.

consumedContracts.name: Durable ingestion and replay
consumedContracts.purpose: Serialize admission, expose durable event identity and safely recycle only fully resolved segments.

boundary.internal: Private Arrow/Lance physical row encoding, receipt lookup, single-table commit, current generation, revision checks and tombstone matching. No other story obtains a direct mutation handle.

adjacentBoundaries.internal: Private lifecycle state machine, directory canonicalization and OS ownership guard. Public v1 types describe the final service; incremental builds must report unsupported/not-ready behavior explicitly rather than accept unimplemented work. Module-local model dispatch serialization is private to this foundation and covers all callers, including read embeddings.

Private segment framing, append/fsync scheduling, checkpoint replacement, tail recovery and disk accounting. Producer source keys are retained through authoritative store receipts; queue recycling alone never authorizes forgetting retry identity.

Private bounded source-context expansion, slot normalization, candidate retrieval, authority and equivalence classification, fidelity checks and serial model scheduling. No normalization result becomes active before the guarded store commit.
Private exact/lexical/vector ranking, mandatory-directive selection, generation-keyed caches and budget packing. Inspect and search share project binding and deletion filters.

Private local-socket framing, connection limits, version handshake, transport cancellation and process signal handling in the executable only. Embedded API import installs no handlers. Remote client disconnect never stops the server.

Private insrc registry binding, temporary-execution refusal, host provider translation and managed turn ownership. VS Code/JetBrains/MCP remain IPC clients; backend integration does not expose index/LMDB handles to the package. This story owns the explicit host admission/coordination design for daemon and memory model work; no existing global scheduler is assumed.

Private CLI-version qualification, trusted hook bootstrap, incremental transcript parser, local spool qualification and capability reporting. Adapter installation requires explicit host configuration; user approval and tool transcripts are not promoted to standing directives.

Private retention planning, purge accounting, Lance version cleanup, migrations, source-qualified lesson proposals and corpus evaluation orchestration. No maintenance timer writes outside the command/worker path.

nonFunctional.performance: Bound source expansion, event size, pending disk bytes, candidate counts, model timeouts, IPC frames and context token budgets. Queue acceptance latency measures append+fsync separately from semantic commit latency. Initial target is bounded memory and nonblocking request handling; p50/p95 acceptance, commit, recall and cold-open thresholds must be measured on named hardware/corpus in LLDs before release. Accuracy takes precedence over throughput. Embedding/model calls are serial; cached reads perform no inference.
nonFunctional.security: Project/session binding and eligibility before enqueue; per-request scope validation and local endpoint access restrictions. No raw prompts/queue content in routine logs. Memory is subordinate context; no hidden reasoning, credentials or automatic cloud REST. Different projects and directories remain isolated. Temp/session-memory execution restrictions remain enforced in insrc and explicit equivalent policy is required of other hosts.
nonFunctional.observability: Bounded metadata: operation/event identity, project pseudonym, queue backlog/oldest age, processing stage/retries, generation, duration, privacy-safe failure code and capture/delivery capability state. Distinguish unavailable/empty, accepted/committed, prepared/delivered, logical delete/physical cleanup. Provide explicit inspection rather than routine payload logging.
nonFunctional.durability: No acknowledged event loss in the supported crash model; at-least-once replay with idempotent committed effects. OS process death, partial writes, fsync failure, lost IPC replies, commit-before-ack, ownership contention and shutdown require fault-injection evidence. Disk/controller failure outside the qualified fsync contract and external native transcript/backups have explicit limits. Lance atomicity/reader freshness are mandatory s3 evidence gates, not assumptions.

api.name: MemoryStore.commit

parameters.name: plan
parameters.purpose: Immutable bounded private plan containing operationId, scope, expectedGeneration, admitted QueueFrame provenance/epoch/hash, per-target revision preconditions, a terminal disposition and validated domain rows. Store generates receipt/control rows; caller cannot supply those.

returns.meaning: Existing identical terminal receipt or a complete committed disposition. Invalid plans throw without partial effects; uncertain native writes fence the writer until reopen/reconciliation.

errors.condition: Unsafe/oversized plan, duplicate rowId, illegal kind or caller-supplied control/receipt, missing revision precondition or invalid references/vector.
Identity/hash/scope/epoch conflict, stale generation/revision or deleted/superseded target.
Uncertain write/manifest/receipt mismatch; fence and require reopen, never blindly retry effects.
Bounded pending-call/row/byte ownership exhausted before mutation.

preconditions: Caller is the module's sole private writer capability; future S4/S9 use it only through admitted queue frames, never IPC/raw user rows.
S1 canonical ownership is held; schema/store UUID/embedding metadata match; frame identity and canonical payload hash are recomputed using S2 codecs.
Native LanceDB0.40.0 standard-path single-table commit is qualified on supported Node22/APFS/ext4 before production wiring.

BroadForgetBarrierV1 is checked against admitted frame and all source dependencies before publication, including unknown IDs; validated provenance is derived by AdmittedProvenanceV1. No model-owned row supplies source authority.
Vector-bearing plan.embeddingProfile must equal model/dimension/normalizationVersion persisted in marker/root and the runtime constant; mismatch never triggers implicit re-embedding.
postconditions: Within the writer lane, refresh latest, validate identity receipt first, then expected generation/revisions/tombstones and references, freeze all outgoing rows, and issue exactly one mergeInsert on rowId with update/insert and no blanket delete or LSM mode.

Exact committed retry returns original receipt before stale-generation handling and adds no rows/version. Conflicting receipt cannot mask a retained accepted identity (S2's invariant remains enforced).
One global control generation advances with effects+receipt; a no-effect terminal failure/quarantine still atomically records its outcome. Cleanup-pending means logical completion only.
Writer lane is released before any queue.markResolved. The store never calls the queue; the future worker/test harness performs acknowledgement afterward.

api.name: MemoryStore.receipt
api.signature: receipt(scope: Scope, operationId: string): Promise<OperationReceipt | null>;

parameters.name: scope
parameters.purpose: Validated requested project/session/branch/environment visibility and current binding epoch.

returns.meaning: Minimal authorized terminal receipt or verified absence. Unavailable storage/proof is an error, never absence.

errors.condition: Malformed request or hidden/unknown operation; outward status handling keeps hidden and missing indistinguishable.

preconditions: Read through the store facade; no raw Table/Connection escapes.
Scope is bound under current HostPolicy; exact receipt identity/hash/epoch data remains internally available for queue verification.
postconditions: No payload/current-memory text leaks via status.
Receipt lookup is usable before inference and after a lost commit/queue acknowledgement; failure does not authorize repeated semantic effects.

api.name: MemoryStore.snapshot

parameters.name: scope
parameters.purpose: Bind scope and epoch for a read-only lease.

returns.meaning: Opaque in-process lease containing version/generation plus bound scope digest, epoch and eligibility time. Registered read handle is distinct from the writer.

preconditions: Acquire latest version and generation together, then pin that exact version on a fresh table handle; never checkout the shared writer.
postconditions: Copying/forging/cross-instance reuse of a snapshot does not acquire authority; store validates its private lease registration.
Lease expiry/release closes its handle. Proposed private limits:16 concurrent leases and30s lifetime; measure before production and expose no new public option.

api.name: MemoryStore.current
api.signature: current(scope: Scope, snapshot: CommittedSnapshot): Promise<readonly MemoryView[]>;

parameters.name: scope
parameters.purpose: Must match the lease's qualified scope/binding.

parameters.name: snapshot
parameters.purpose: Registered pinned view; consumed/released after this projection or explicit private lifecycle release.

returns.meaning: Validated current eligible views from one version, with mandatory scope/tombstone/lifecycle/time filters and deterministic id ordering. No semantic ranking or context packing.

errors.condition: Generation or binding changed before final read linearization check; retry on a new snapshot.
Private result bound exceeded; never silently truncate.

preconditions: Validate epoch before query and at return; apply project/qualifier visibility before collecting candidates.
Use pinned-version current/revision/evidence/source/tombstone data; exclude any record derived from a forgotten/expired source before returning a view.
postconditions: Final latest-generation/epoch check linearizes the read. A deletion completed before that check prevents an old snapshot from returning deleted content.
Re-evaluate validity at current time even when generation is unchanged; publish earliest validity boundary to future S5 read facade/cache integration.
Bound output to4096 rows for this enumeration API; future S5 uses bounded store read predicates/projections, not an unbounded full-store dump.

api.name: ReceiptVerifier
api.signature: byIdentity(identity: StableIdentity): Promise<ReceiptLookup>; byOperation(operationId: string, requestedScope: Scope): Promise<ReceiptLookup>; confirmRetirement(reference: RetirementReference): Promise<boolean>;

returns.meaning: Minimal authoritative proof with operation/identity/hash/scope/epoch/generation/event receipt and queueTerminal, or distinguished absence/unavailability. Retirement confirmation returns only a matching boolean.

errors.condition: Storage/validation cannot prove the requested disposition.

preconditions: Facade is created by S3 and passed to S2 at host composition; queue never imports store implementation.
All reads wait behind active store commits as needed; no callback from the store into the held queue lane.
postconditions: A retained terminal receipt remains verifiable after queue segment unlink and after logical forget.
Receipt/tombstone compaction and producer replay-watermark policy remain S9 obligations; S3 exposes no unsafe deletion shortcut.

api.name: MemoryStore.close

returns.meaning: All admitted store work/read leases settled and owned table/connection handles closed.

errors.condition: Native write or resource release remains unverified; S1 ownership must remain held.

preconditions: Host stops admission before store/queue release; no global timer or process handler installed by import.
postconditions: Never closes host model/policy/logger ports. Native in-flight cancellation does not grant another writer until actual settlement.

api.name: MemoryStore.validateFrameEligibility
api.signature: validateFrameEligibility(frame: QueueFrame): Promise<{ eligible: boolean; rejectedByTombstoneIds: readonly string[] }>;

parameters.name: frame
parameters.purpose: Immutable verified accepted frame, with finalized AdmittedProvenanceV1 metadata; check before future S4 inference.

returns.type: Promise<{ eligible: boolean; rejectedByTombstoneIds: readonly string[] }>
returns.meaning: Read-only minimal current protection result. No table/content/queue handle escapes; eligible is a hint rechecked inside commit, not a future authorization lease.

errors.condition: Frame or barrier authority cannot be verified; never treat unavailable proof as eligibility.
Protection checks cannot be completed within bounded dependency limits.

preconditions: Store ownership/read lease and current epoch verified; no store-to-queue callback.
postconditions: No durable mutation or inference; pending old frames can be terminalized with no effect after broad forgetting.
The writer rechecks barriers and frame provenance atomically before merge; a stale eligible result grants no right to commit.

dataModelChanges.details: Proposed packages/project-memory/src/store/codec.ts owns explicit Arrow schema: rowId:utf8 non-null; rowKind:utf8 non-null; projectId:utf8 non-null; namespaceKey:utf8 non-null; scopeEpoch:utf8 non-null; sessionId/branch/environment:utf8 nullable; entityId/revisionId/sourceId/operationId/payloadHash/identityDigest/generation:utf8 nullable; status:utf8 nullable; validFrom/validUntil timestamps nullable with validated safe millisecond values; payload:utf8 canonical typed JSON non-null; embedding:FixedSizeList<Float32,D> nullable. Validate envelope/payload agreement and finite exactly-D vectors. Persist integers/identities/generation as bounded decimal/hex strings; canonical payload preserves -0/Unicode. No implicit schema inference, remote URI, RTE/LSM write spec or embedding callback. Package pins @lancedb/lancedb0.40.0 and apache-arrow18.1.0 independently; root backend modules are not dependencies. MemoryStore owns exactly one table named records under canonical dataDirectory/memory.lance.

Own sc4 refinement keeps operationId/scope/expectedGeneration/rows and adds immutable admitted QueueFrame provenance, scopeEpoch, commandHash, per-current expectedRevision map and disposition. Generated receipt/control rows are never accepted from callers; domain IDs use kind-prefixed SHA256 of qualified namespace and logical keys, with exact duplicate rowIds rejected. All writes are serialized; uniqueness is application-enforced because Lance primary keys are unenforced. Refresh writer before guards; targeted duplicate-count checks plus bounded streaming metadata/ID validation at open fail closed. Proposed private safety caps:64 pending calls,4096 effect rows and min(64MiB,8*maxEventBytes) canonical batch bytes, with measured native RSS/allocation limits disclosed. Over-limit plans fail before mutation; no partial chunked event commits. Future worker can explicitly terminalize an invalid plan via a separate validated no-effect failure disposition for the same admitted event, not by bypassing guards. Vector-bearing plans additionally require the private embeddingProfile metadata in EmbeddingCompatibilityV1; the runtime constant and root/marker must match exactly. [c14,c23]

Exactly one current row per qualified memory key; rowId includes project/epoch/scope and memoryId. Payload holds kind/text/status, revision and provenance links. Update requires snapshot generation plus per-target expected revision; frame.command.expectedRevision, when supplied, must also match. S4 supplies semantics/slot selection; S3 only validates exact keys, transitions, allowed scope and references. No implicit scope broadening: promotion requires a newly authorized command at the intended scope. Current -> revision is 1:1; memory -> immutable revisions is 1:many. Supersession links validated same namespace; no cycles or dangling active references.

Immutable Revision rows belong to one qualified Memory; SourceSpan rows identify admitted source occurrences/version; Evidence rows join exactly one revision and one source span (many-to-many through evidence). Stable rowId/domain prefixes avoid collisions. Reject reference rewrites, scope/epoch mismatch, missing or tombstoned dependencies. Source payload retention and policy redaction are explicit; forgetting hides dependent current/provenance/derived rows without claiming physical removal of old versions. Arbitrary evidence inference/resolution is S4, not this store.

One immutable authoritative receipt per stable project-producer-event identity, containing identityDigest, full admitted-command hash, complete visibility scope/epoch, operationId/eventId, terminal state, generation and queueTerminal. Store generates it in the same mutation as effects and control. Correcting/forgetting a memory never rewrites an old event receipt; exact replay returns that outcome without reactivating content. Store unavailable is not absent. No raw transcript in routine logs; producer identities may need retention beyond queue recycling and cannot be falsely claimed physically erased.

Minimal monotone protection row for a qualified memory/source/subject lifecycle and delete generation. A source tombstone invalidates any current/revision/evidence/derived view referencing that source; exact scalar scope and reference checks must execute before ranking/limits or projection. Deleted logical identifiers are never resurrected by a different delayed event; new activity requires a new authorized lifecycle identifier under explicit policy, not tombstone removal. Supersession/correction creates immutable lineage with current-pointer change atomically; expiry uses validity intervals and current-time filtering. Physical purge/version retention/migrations are S9; no optimize/prune/drop/reset API is exposed by S3. BroadForgetBarrierV1 below extends exact-target guards to project, source session and source conversation lifecycles, including unknown IDs from pending frames. Matching is against admitted provenance before inference/commit and on read dependencies. [c14,c21]

Store-generated root control row owns schema version, store UUID, embedding model/dimension and monotonically increasing uint64 generation. Namespace epoch controls are scoped. One global generation is deliberately conservative: any commit invalidates outstanding current-read tokens/caches, including other projects. CommittedSnapshot pins a distinct read handle at version plus generation, scope digest and current epoch; handles are process-owned leases, not serializable authorization. A final head-generation/epoch check rejects stale snapshot results, while eligibility time is re-evaluated without a write. Sorted rowId streaming at open uses SDK orderBy with small batches to identify duplicate IDs without a JS full-database map; benchmark native sort/scan memory/time before release. The normalizationVersion field is mandatory and checked separately from semantic ProcessingVersion.normalizer; see EmbeddingCompatibilityV1. [c14,c23]

Reserve rowKind delivery and qualified storage envelope/reference fields, but no capture/delivery handshake, success reporting or protocol semantics are introduced. S8 owns its domain schema; unsupported delivery writes/read projections remain NOT_READY until that schema is supplied and qualified. S3 defines only that future derived references are scope/epoch qualified and subject to tombstone/validity checks, and that any eventual delivery effect uses the same writer.

Proposed store files are packages/project-memory/src/store/types.ts, packages/project-memory/src/store/codec.ts, packages/project-memory/src/store/guards.ts, packages/project-memory/src/store/lance-store.ts, packages/project-memory/src/store/writer.ts, packages/project-memory/src/store/reads.ts, packages/project-memory/src/store/receipts.ts; packages/project-memory/src/host-node.ts composes under existing DirectoryOwnership. Import stays pure/lazy. Fresh initialization is allowed only when the owned root contains solely recognized S1 layout/lock metadata: persist a private S3 store-format.json initialization intent with UUID/schema/embedding metadata, create one local memory.lance/records table and root control generation0, then durably mark ready before queue creation/service readiness. This marker is format/init evidence, never an alternate memory/receipt authority. Existing matching S3 marker+database is reopened and validated; interrupted generation0 initialization is resumed only when provably recognized, without deleting unknown files. A missing/corrupt store in any non-pristine root, including an existing S2 queue-only directory, returns NOT_READY/STORE_UNAVAILABLE and preserves queue bytes; no automatic empty-store upgrade or sidecar deletion fallback is permitted. S9 owns an explicitly reviewed additive migration for such development directories. Normal open order is S1 owner -> qualified S3 store -> queue with receipt facade -> queue recovery -> service. Store never opens or acknowledges the queue itself. Close drains all owned reads/writes and retains S1 guard if settlement/cleanup is uncertain. S3 adds no semantic worker/public context: submit remains accepted, operation can reconcile receipts, context/search/inspect remain NOT_READY until S5. No remote URI, backend singleton, index path or reset API; private directory identity/permissions are checked before and after native operations. S3 also composes the private AdmissionTransforms hooks described in AdmittedProvenanceV1; this is an explicit policy-output behavior requirement with unchanged public TypeScript and S2 frame shapes. Existing host/test policy fixtures and README must be updated; identity-echo policy alone cannot assert source authority. QueueAdmission's new trusted hook seam is the explicit private integration change; host-policy errors remain sanitized. [c16,c21]

S3 owns validated scalar eligibility, not ranking. Read scopes enumerate at most eight allowed namespace hashes (stored qualifiers absent or equal to requested qualifiers); predicates are built from validated internal hex IDs, never caller SQL. Effect scopes must be within the admitted command's scope authority (same or narrower, never broader); explicit project/source forget selectors are constrained to that authorized namespace subtree. The private read facade resolves scope/epoch/status/validity and tombstoned source/revision dependencies before any vector top-k limit. It can supply eligible IDs/projections to future S5 without exposing a native Table. Bound the entire eligibility/dependency work set (proposed4096 current rows and16384 dependency/tombstone references); if it cannot prove eligibility within those limits return CONTEXT_OVERFLOW rather than post-filtering a truncated ANN result. Embedding dimension is an explicit matched metadata value with proposed safety range1..8192, not inferred from data. Measure these private bounds before release; no production SLO is claimed.

Normative private storage schema for S3; public v1 types do not change. Each physical row has exactly one discriminated payload below. Codec rejects unknown fields, unknown enums, missing required fields, unsafe numbers, duplicate set members, envelope/payload disagreements and unresolved references. Optional values are explicit null in canonical JSON, not undefined. All IDs are bounded nonempty strings (at most512 UTF-8 bytes), hashes are lowercase SHA256 hex64; generation/revision counters are canonical uint64 decimal strings. Text is nonempty and all strings/arrays remain within the existing canonical depth/node and batch byte/row limits; no silent truncation. Times are safe integer epoch milliseconds, createdAt<=updatedAt and validity is [validFrom,validUntil), with either bound null. IDs of all referenced domain rows include their namespace/epoch. A row cannot reference another namespace even when project IDs match. The tuple source identity is the admitted S2 identity; store derives attribution only from the policy-admitted QueueFrame. S4 chooses assertion meaning/authority classification, S3 validates these storage shapes and trusted provenance.

Common definitions: Lifecycle = candidate|active|conflicted|superseded|expired|deleted; Kind = directive|fact|decision|progress|lesson; ProcessingVersion = {processor:string, normalizer:string|null, prompt:string|null, schema:1}, with all version strings bounded/nonempty when present. Normalizer/prompt may be null only for deterministic non-LLM operations; capture/correct/resolve that emit memory revisions require both. Authority = {origin:user|host-policy|artifact|assistant|tool|document, sourceIds:string[], policyVersion:string}; sourceIds must name admitted source rows backing the claimed origin and policyVersion is admitted metadata, never inferred from confidence. Assertion = {subject:string, category:string, predicate:string, value:Json, polarity:positive|negative, conditions:Json[]}; value/conditions are bounded canonical structured data supplied by S4, whose domain interpretation is versioned, not arbitrary envelope keys. No scalar authority score is a privilege grant. Receipt additionally requires rejectedByTombstoneIds:string[] (empty unless a no-effect failure was caused by existing protection); current/root control queueId semantics follow BroadForgetBarrierV1. Source references in memory are derived from Evidence, not independent mutable counters.

Current payload = {schemaVersion:1, memoryId:string, kind:Kind, assertion:Assertion, text:string, scope:Scope, authority:Authority, status:Lifecycle, revisionId:string, createdAt:number, updatedAt:number, validFrom:number|null, validUntil:number|null, sourceIds:string[], relatedMemoryIds:string[], supersedesMemoryId:string|null}. Revision payload = {schemaVersion:1, revisionId:string, memoryId:string, predecessorRevisionId:string|null, mutationReason:{code:create|evidence-added|correct|conflict|resolve|supersede|expire|forget, explanation:string}, sourceEvent:{operationId:string, identityDigest:string, payloadHash:string}, processingVersion:ProcessingVersion, committedGeneration:string, createdAt:number, snapshot:CurrentPayload}. The revision snapshot must equal its corresponding new current payload; first revision predecessor is null, later predecessor is exactly the guarded previous revision. History rows are immutable; duplicate existing revision IDs must be byte-identical or fail. Text/assertion/authority/related IDs and sources in a revision are complete values, never partial patches. Revision counters are not used as revision identity.

Source payload = {schemaVersion:1, sourceId:string, identity:{producerId:string,eventId:string,sessionId:string,turnId:string,sourceVersion:string}, operationId:string, contentHash:string, attribution:{origin:Authority.origin, policyVersion:string}, span:{unit:utf8-byte, start:number, end:number}, location:{kind:admitted-excerpt, text:string}|{kind:durable-reference, reference:string}, occurredAt:number|null, admittedAt:number, validFrom:number|null, validUntil:number|null}. Span bounds are safe integers with 0<=start<end; excerpt spans fit the admitted UTF-8 content; durable references are inert locators, never fetched by S3. ContentHash/attribution/time are derived and checked by the exact AdmittedProvenanceV1 contract below; occurredAt is null when the host cannot attest it. Source records are immutable. Evidence payload = {schemaVersion:1, evidenceId:string, memoryId:string, revisionId:string, sourceId:string, sourceContentHash:string, relation:supports|contradicts, createdByOperationId:string}. Each Evidence references exactly one matching revision and one source; each revision and each source can have zero or many Evidence rows. Key is deterministic over qualified revision/source/relation, so reprocessing an occurrence cannot multiply support. Every sourceId on a current/revision/authority must be represented in its Evidence set; each Evidence's sourceContentHash must equal the referenced Source. Authority sources must be a subset of the revision's provenance. Lifecycle-only revisions carry new Evidence rows for the carried sources; no implicit history reference suppresses eligibility validation.

Receipt payload = {schemaVersion:1, operationId:string, eventId:string, identityDigest:string, payloadHash:string, scope:Scope, scopeEpoch:string, state:committed|failed|quarantined|cleanup-pending, generation:string, queueTerminal:true, affectedRevisions:{memoryId:string, previousRevisionId:string|null, revisionId:string}[], sourceIds:string[], tombstoneIds:string[], processingVersion:ProcessingVersion, errorCode:MemoryFailureCode|null, committedAt:number}. Store derives affectedRevisions from exactly the current/revision changes, and sourceIds/tombstoneIds from inserted effects, sorts by qualified ID, rejects duplicates and verifies all in-batch or already-committed dependencies. committed requires errorCode null; failed/quarantined require an error code and no domain effects; cleanup-pending denotes successful logical forgetting/maintenance with tombstones, not native uncertainty. New captures never claim cleanup-pending. The public OperationReceipt is a minimal projection; no authority/provenance/payload leaks. Terminal receipt is immutable and survives later revisions/deletion; affectedRevisions are historical references, not a requirement that their content remain recallable. Accepted/processing are queue/runtime states, never fabricated terminal storage receipts.

Tombstone payload = {schemaVersion:1, tombstoneId:string, selector:{kind:memory, memoryId:string}|{kind:source, sourceId:string}|{kind:subject, subjectKeyHash:string}|{kind:session, sessionId:string}|{kind:conversation, producerId:string, sessionId:string}|{kind:project}, namespaceKey:string, scopeEpoch:string, invalidFromGeneration:string, queueId:string, cutoffSequence:string, mode:closed-lifecycle, createdByOperationId:string, createdAt:number}. Exactly one selector; store derives the subject hash using the versioned canonical subject/category tuple and qualifies it by the authorized namespace. No forgotten text, reason prose or raw assertion is persisted in the marker. Markers are monotone/immutable. Subject markers cover that authorized namespace subtree without broadening scope. Session/conversation/project markers follow BroadForgetBarrierV1 below; their project-wide authority must be explicit. cutoffSequence is the forgetting frame's durable queue sequence, not a wall-clock time or largest currently-known memory ID. A different lifecycle must have a different qualified identifier and explicit admitted authority; delayed events cannot recreate a tombstoned identity.

Control payload is a strict union: root = {schemaVersion:1, kind:root, storeId:string, generation:string, embeddingModel:string, embeddingDimension:number, normalizationVersion:string, queueId:string|null, createdAt:number}; namespace = {schemaVersion:1, kind:namespace, namespaceKey:string, scope:Scope, scopeEpoch:string, createdAt:number}. Root has one deterministic row ID; namespace identity is immutable and a changed host epoch creates a different namespace, never rewrites prior authorization. Only store-generated control/receipts are accepted. Delivery payload has no v1 accepted schema in S3: reads/writes of delivery domain data return NOT_READY until S8. Unsupported schemaVersion returns UNSUPPORTED_VERSION without mutation. The initialization marker contains only {format:insrc-project-memory-store, version:1, storeId:string, embeddingModel:string, embeddingDimension:number, normalizationVersion:string, state:initializing|ready}; the database control is the sole generation authority. [c1,c3,c5,c14]

Allowed current-memory transitions are explicit. Absent->candidate or active only with create reason and an admitted capture/correct/resolve event, source provenance and no matching tombstone; the first revision predecessor is null. candidate->candidate/active/conflicted/superseded/expired/deleted; active->active/conflicted/superseded/expired/deleted; conflicted->conflicted/active/superseded/expired/deleted. The terminal statuses superseded/expired/deleted never return to an eligible status under the same memory lifecycle; deleted has a matching monotone tombstone. An unchanged terminal row is permitted only as an exact no-op replay, never a new material revision. Every material transition including active->active produces an immutable revision and advances the current pointer atomically. Reasons are checked: create only on absent; evidence-added preserves assertion/text/authority/status except derived source set; correct requires kind correct and an eligible prior target plus revision guard; conflict sets conflicted; resolve requires kind resolve and candidate/conflicted target; supersede sets superseded and has a valid acyclic replacement link; expire sets expired only at/past validUntil; forget sets deleted and publishes target/source/subject tombstone. A forget may cover multiple eligible states; already terminal content can receive a tombstone without rewriting its immutable history. A no-op exact receipt retry bypasses new transition guards, not tombstone visibility. Scope/authority may never be promoted implicitly; changed lifecycle/scope requires a separately admitted new identity. Expiry eligibility is time-based immediately even before a maintenance event materializes expired status. Malformed transition rejects before mutation; S4 supplies the chosen semantic action and S9 supplies future maintenance commands through the same private writer. [c1,c3,c5,c14]

Add a private StoreOwnedWork adapter in proposed packages/project-memory/src/store/lifecycle.ts implementing existing runtime OwnedWork without changing public MemoryStore. host-node.ts composes [queue, storeOwnedWork], in that dependency order. stopAdmission(): synchronous/idempotent; reject new commit/snapshot/current requests, stop lease creation and signal cancellation to active facade reads; already admitted native writes and receipt-proof operations remain tracked until actual settlement. Queue-facing ReceiptVerifier remains callable during queue drain/close so a held queue lane can complete; stopping store mutation admission never makes receipt reads falsely absent. pending(): count queued/active writes, in-flight receipt/native reads and unreleased reader leases once each; never report zero while native work or close is unverified. drain(): wait writer-tail and all admitted reads; promptly release idle leases, await active queries before closing their handles, and enforce lease deadlines; no new commits, queue callback or owner release. close(): after queue.close, stop new receipt proof admission, wait any proof already started, close all remaining read/table/connection handles exactly once. Reject STORE_UNAVAILABLE on any uncertain settlement; do not release S1 ownership. A drain timeout is only a caller deadline and never authorizes closing/releasing an in-flight writer.

Existing runtime.ts already stops all participants, drains them serially, waits models and closes in array order while retaining ownership on failures. Preserve that order: stop queue ingress -> stop new store mutations/leases -> queue drain (proofs still available) -> store drain -> models idle -> queue.close (may seal) -> store.close -> owner.close. On the first event commit, root control binds queueId from the admitted frame if still null; all later commits must use that same queueId. A different queue identity in an existing store is STORE_UNAVAILABLE pending explicit S9 migration, never a fresh replay domain. This bootstrap binding is generated inside the first event mutation, not a callback into queue. Timestamps and store generation do not replace the durable ingress sequence.

Target semantics: memory matches one qualified memory lifecycle; source matches one qualified source occurrence and all its derivatives; subject matches the qualified canonical subject/category hash and descendants already defined. session matches SourceIdentity.sessionId across producers in this project/epoch. conversation matches the tuple {producerId,SourceIdentity.sessionId}; this source conversation identifier is distinct from Scope.sessionId, which is a visibility qualifier. project matches every source/current/derived record in projectId/epoch, regardless of visibility qualifiers. The session/conversation/project forget commands require an unqualified project Scope (no sessionId/branch/environment) and explicit HostPolicy authorization of that exact selector, because their derivatives may have been promoted into project-level namespaces. A narrower command is POLICY_DENIED rather than silently broadening its visibility. A session visibility namespace can separately be targeted by existing exact-memory/source selection; there is no ambiguous conflation of source-session and visibility-session identifiers.

All broad markers use mode closed-lifecycle: they invalidate every matching committed view and reject ALL subsequent effect plans from that old source/project lifecycle, both sequence<=cutoff and sequence>cutoff. Thus a not-yet-processed pre-forget frame cannot invent unseen memoryId/sourceId/subjectKeyHash to escape the barrier. The queue cutoff records the causal boundary and permits explicit tests/audit; a larger sequence is NOT itself permission to reactivate. Store guards check both frame origin against matching broad barriers and every planned/current revision's entire source dependency set. Barrier-aware eligibility filters existing stored Source rows and derived records, even if the current memory lives at broader visibility. An unbounded dependency/barrier set fails CONTEXT_OVERFLOW rather than truncating and leaking erased content. Schema validation of control plans precedes barrier matching; the forget event itself can publish another monotone marker and terminal receipt without recalling or recreating the targeted content.

testLevels.purpose: AC29/ac3 isolation scenario matrix with explicit S3 evidence and supporting-story completion gates; no new reset API.
fixturesNeeded: Common oracle: two independently owned temporary databases at canonical sibling paths, a real S3 committed memory/revision/source/receipt/tombstone set and one real accepted unacknowledged S2 queue frame. Record logical row IDs/payload digests/generation/receipt proofs and exact pending-frame identity/hash/bytes; record unrelated graph/vector entities in a temporary index. Reopen both sides after every operation; compare logical data, not mutable Lance directory mtimes.

S3/backend test-only harness exercises the existing Indexer full rebuild path (which deletes repository entities via deleteEntitiesForRepo) against a tiny registered temporary repository and isolated test storage. Assert committed memory generation/content/deletion guards/proofs and pending frame digest/accepted status survive, while expected index rows are rebuilt. Also exercise the existing isolated index-store reset/removal helper where available, then rebuild/reopen and repeat the memory/queue oracle. Never import backend storage into the standalone package runtime, and never touch the user's live index. A sentinel alone is insufficient.

Memory-side S3 owns qualified path authority and store reopen/refusal, not memory reset/physical purge. S3 tests exercise a private, non-destructive cleanup-target preflight with memory.lance as candidate; root, queue, parent/child overlap, symlink aliases, changed inode and unknown/foreign paths reject before any unlink. Canonical absolute target must be strictly inside the owned root, equal to the owned memory.lance database, and disjoint in both containment directions from root metadata and queue files. Control/receipt guards still forbid actually deleting memory.lance as an S3 operation. This private preflight is not a public reset endpoint or permission to erase replay protection.

S9 support gate defines the real memory reset/cleanup scenario: use only its approved queued maintenance path, preserve/recreate required receipt/tombstone replay barriers atomically, retain the admitted pending event, verify unrelated index graph/vector contents unchanged, and reopen/replay without duplicate effects. Run with committed content plus history, receipts and pending work. Until S9 implements and passes this scenario, full AC29 is explicitly pending; S3 must not report reset/physical cleanup or full epic AC29 complete.

Cross-host overlap support gate (S1/S7 host binding): actual index directory may not be known to standalone MemoryOptions. Backend host must reject equal, ancestor, descendant and symlink-equivalent memory/index/queue cleanup roots before open/destruction, then recheck canonical identity before cleanup. S3 proves internal memory/queue separation and exposes no index deletion operation; S7 tests the actual backend guard, and S9 invokes it for cleanup. Document both pending integration gates in S3 completion evidence rather than turn an index sentinel into an AC29 pass.

Each scenario records platform/source/SDK fingerprints, operation invoked, pre/post logical memory+index state and pending-event receipt/hash. Unsupported future operation is NOT_READY/pending coverage, never a skip counted as a pass. AC3 mapping is complete as a plan; closure evidence must distinguish S3-qualified behavior from S1/S7/S9-dependent AC29 coverage.

alternativesConsidered.name: Tagged rows with canonical typed JSON payloads
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: One explicit Arrow table, small shared scalar envelope, validated per-kind payloads and nullable embeddings.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Refine sc4 inside the standalone package. One current row per qualified memory key, immutable revision/source/evidence rows, minimal receipts/tombstones/control/delivery rows share records.lance. Runtime codecs validate the discriminated domain payload before serializing canonical JSON; common scope/identity/revision/lifecycle columns support safe predicates. The sole store writer prepares a complete event batch and performs one standard-path mergeInsert, including its generated receipt and generation. Separate per-read handles pin a committed table version; no second authoritative index or backend connection.
pros: Smallest physical schema meeting the approved typed-row single-table commit contract
Reuses the package's canonical bounded JSON and receipt-matching invariants without backend imports
Adding kind-specific fields need not widen every Arrow row
cons: Payload validation/decoding and exact referential checks remain application responsibilities
Scalar hot fields must be duplicated consistently in envelope and payload or derived once
Crash durability, null vectors and read snapshots still require actual platform qualification

alternativesConsidered.name: Wide Arrow schema with per-kind typed structures
alternativesConsidered.oneLineSummary: The same single-table atomic contract with Arrow struct columns for every row kind.
alternativesConsidered.approach: Keep one table and single writer, but encode current/revision/source/evidence/receipt/tombstone/control/delivery payloads as nullable Arrow structs with a rowKind discriminator. One batch merge contains all effects and generated receipt/control rows; version-pinned reads use the same contract. Arrow checks physical types, while store guards still enforce identity, scope, expected revision, lifecycle and deletion. No multi-table or backend store is introduced.
pros: More physical typing and potential direct scalar projection of nested fields
Identical event atomicity and read-snapshot boundary
cons: Wider sparse schema couples all payload changes and migrations to every table row
Cross-language/native struct compatibility requires a larger qualification matrix
Does not remove application-level authorization, referential or deletion checks
alternativesConsidered.reasonRejected: Conceptually valid but wider schema and migration coupling are unnecessary.

erDefinition.narrative: Typed rows share one physical table. Each Revision and each SourceSpan has zero or many Evidence rows; each Evidence holds exactly one required revisionId and sourceId. Parent-to-child edges are drawn once, and scalar foreign-key fields state exact endpoints without contradictory one-to-one reverse edges. CurrentRevisionId selects one entry from the memory's immutable history. [c1,c14]

StoreControl.description: One root schema/generation control row per owned physical memory database.

namespaces.description: Scoped namespace controls owned by this database.

normalizationVersion.description: Package-controlled embedding input/Float32 normalization recipe, distinct from semantic extraction versions; must match marker/runtime/plan.

Namespace.description: Qualified project/epoch/scope, stored as control metadata; owns all logical identifiers in that namespace.

memories.description: Zero or more current memories owned by the namespace.

sources.description: Zero or more immutable source occurrences.

receipts.description: Retained event outcomes; many receipts may affect the same memory.

tombstones.description: Monotone deletion guards retained for replay protection.

CurrentMemory.description: One current pointer per qualified memory identifier.

currentRevisionId.description: Exactly one current Revision ID; must name a revision in this memory's owned history.

supersedesMemoryId.description: Optional same-namespace predecessor ID; acyclic. Multiple replacements may reference one historical memory; not a one-to-one relation.

Revision.description: One immutable revision owned by one logical memory.

evidence.description: Evidence joins to the sources used for this revision.

SourceSpan.description: An immutable admitted source occurrence/version, separate from canonical memory.

evidence.description: A source supports zero or many Evidence rows; each row has exactly one sourceId. Independent of revision ownership.

Evidence.description: An associative row linking one revision to one source; provides many-to-many provenance.

revisionId.description: Required foreign key to exactly one same-namespace Revision; validated against Revision.evidence ownership.

sourceId.description: Required foreign key to exactly one same-namespace SourceSpan; validated against SourceSpan.evidence inverse collection.

ProcessingReceipt.description: Immutable terminal outcome for exactly one event identity; survives queue recycling.

rowId.description: Qualified receipt identifier derived from stable event identity.

operationId.description: Stable event operation identifier, not a transport request id.

Tombstone.description: A monotone qualified logical deletion guard; does not promise physical purge.

selector.description: Exclusive memory/source/subject/source-session/source-conversation/project selector; broad lifecycle guards also cover unseen IDs. Payload union is authoritative.

queueId.description: Durable queue identity of the authorized forget frame; bound to store root on first event commit.

cutoffSequence.description: Forget frame ingress sequence; higher sequence alone never reopens the closed lifecycle.

sequenceDefinition.narrative: S3 opens the authoritative store before queue recovery and publishes event effects, receipt and generation in one mutation. Queue acknowledgement follows release of the store lane; pinned reads check freshness before returning. Shutdown stops new mutations but keeps proof reads alive until the queue is drained/closed; partial startup uses the same dependency order. Admission uses pure module transforms outside the host error boundary, preserving module validation/conflict codes while sanitizing host failures. Store initialization and vector plans check a persisted embedding normalization version. Broad-forget barriers block unseen pending effects and are rechecked at commit; later sequence alone never reopens a closed lifecycle.

messages.label: Open qualified store under held ownership
messages.description: Fail closed for non-pristine missing stores; validate metadata and generation. Validate model, dimension and embedding normalizationVersion across marker/root/runtime before queue recovery.

messages.label: Open queue with store receipt verifier
messages.description: Recover only after receipt authority is available.

messages.label: Submit raw untrusted source envelope
messages.description: Raw producer payload cannot contain admitted or policyAttestation fields; command identity is fixed.

messages.label: Run module validation, then trusted host policy
messages.description: Module validateInput executes outside host try/catch. Only the original host admit callback is sanitized; missing attestation is checked by trusted finalize afterward.

messages.label: Return finalized admitted payload
messages.description: Module finalize/snapshot/envelope checks occur outside host catch. FileQueue persist detects genuine historical conflicts outside that catch too; host-thrown errors remain sanitized.

messages.label: Return durably accepted receipt
messages.description: No semantic store effect is implied by durable queue acceptance.

messages.label: Reconcile retained/replayed identity
messages.description: Proof must agree with retained frame hash, scope and epoch.

messages.label: Read admitted frame
messages.description: No semantic normalization implementation is introduced in S3.

messages.label: Check current broad lifecycle barriers
messages.description: Before future S4 inference. Closed target yields no-effect failed receipt. Commit always rechecks; preflight eligibility never bypasses a later forget.

messages.label: Commit immutable bounded plan
messages.description: Existing exact receipt is checked before stale generation; validate authority, revisions and tombstones.

messages.label: One merge: effects + receipt + generation
messages.description: No second-table transaction or independent receipt write. A forget publishes closed-lifecycle protection even for IDs not yet known from pending events.

messages.label: Committed version or uncertain outcome
messages.description: Uncertainty fences the lane until settlement and receipt reconciliation.

messages.label: Return receipt; release store lane
messages.description: Store never calls queue; a lost reply is reconciled by durable receipt.

messages.label: Acknowledge committed generation
messages.description: Only after the store lane is released.

messages.label: Verify receipt and retirement proof
messages.description: Queue may wait on store; no reverse callback creates a lock cycle.

messages.label: Pin distinct read handle at committed version
messages.description: Read eligibility uses one version; no checkout on shared writer.

messages.label: Read eligible current rows and dependencies
messages.description: Resolve scope, source tombstones and validity before candidate limits.

messages.label: Final head generation and epoch check
messages.description: Changed head rejects stale content; reevaluate current-time expiry.

messages.label: Authorize return or require retry
messages.description: No old deleted content passes a final check after deletion completion.

messages.label: Stop queue admission; drain proof-dependent work
messages.description: Service OwnedWork array is [queue,storeAdapter]; host also stops new store mutations/leases. Existing receipt callbacks remain available.

messages.label: Drain native writes and reader leases
messages.description: No deadline or cancellation counts as native settlement; pending remains nonzero until work/handles settle.

messages.label: Close queue before store proof admission
messages.description: Seal and close the queue with receipt facade still usable. Startup rollback follows this same order.

messages.label: Close all store handles; then release owner
messages.description: Reject new proofs, settle in-flight reads and close native handles. Attempt both participants' cleanup; retain guard if either is uncertain.
